data.title: Inhibition of the Lysosomal Amino Acid Sensor SLC38A9 by the Membrane Microprotein SPAR
data.authors: Saeher A; Mu X; Gonen T

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Purified SLC38A9 in liposomes (in vitro); docking model
data.finding: In a reconstituted system, the lysosomal microprotein SPAR bound the amino-acid transporter-receptor SLC38A9, inhibited its arginine transport and blocked downstream Rag GTPase recruitment, supported by a docking model. Purified-protein and liposome experiments only; not tested in cells or animals here.
data.abstract_excerpt: Long noncoding RNAs, previously thought to serve no function, have recently been discovered to encode for microproteins that regulate cellular functions. Small regulatory peptide of amino acid response (SPAR) is a microprotein in the lysosome that responds to amino acid availability in the cell. In this study, we investigated the interactions between SPAR and SLC38A9, a lysosomal amino acid transporter and receptor involved in the mechanistic target of rapamycin 1 (mTORC1) pathway. We found that SPAR binds SLC38A9 and inhibits arginine transport in SLC38A9.
